Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap to lock in what we discussed and the next steps so we’re aligned heading into the trial: 

Pain points you called out
- Extraction quality from legacy ticket transcripts (entity drift, inconsistent labels)
- High inference cost at 99th percentile latency for your customer-facing features
- Lack of safe rollouts across regions with data residency constraints

Goals for the 30-day trial
- Validate extraction F1 >= 0.78 on a ~5k prompt test set (we’ll provide an eval harness)
- End-to-end median latency < 120ms for 2k qps simulation on Dedicated pool (demo workload)
- Confirm data flows and access model for EU-region support and audit logs

Proposed trial scope (agreed on call)
- 30-day sandbox on Redwood Dedicated (shared but isolated pool)
- Prompt set: 5k labeled examples + 1k unlabeled for model comparison; Redwood will run baseline evals
- Owners: Chloe (sales PM) / Ben (SE, infra & access) / Lena (Acme data owner)
- Success metrics: F1, 99th pctl latency, and cost per 1k tokens under $X (TBD in SOW)

Access & setup outline (high-level)
1) Acme to provision a read-only S3 bucket (sample transcripts) + service account for Redwood SEs
2) Redwood will provide temporary API keys and a bootstrap config for the Dedicated pool
3) Ben will share a short access checklist and runbook for network allowlists (see attachment)

Attachments I've included: redwood-trial-charter.pdf (scope + timeline) and access-checklist.csv (S3/service account fields).

Next steps (owners & timing)
- Lena: confirm S3 bucket & service account by EOD Wed 6/23
- Ben: send bootstrapping runbook and initial infra checks by Tue 6/22
- Chloe: finalize trial charter + send DocuSign template for the trial terms by Thu 6/24

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll adjust. Otherwise we’ll treat this as the working plan and proceed once the S3/service account is provisioned.

Best,
